subject: Making input object accessible to R session for debugging help?

messages.author: 8ef1ff47b479f1c7
messages.subject: Making input object accessible to R session for debugging help?
parts:
I've recently really started playing more with Shiny and love it. One aspect of extreme frustration is, as you probably know, tracking down bugs or oddities in the code. One thing that would make this *unbelievably* easier would be to somehow make the input object available in the current R session. This way, I could run the code in server.R in my session without having to re-define everything taking an input$var value.

Is there any way to do this? Hopefully what I'm suggesting is clear?

ui.R
==========

sliderInput(inputId = "var1", label = "var1",
                min = 0, max = 50, value = c(10, 25), step = 5),

sliderInput(inputId = "var2", label = "var2",
                min = 0, max = 50, value = c(10, 25), step = 5),
...
==========


server.R
==========

lapply(something, function (x) {
  expand.grid(seq(min(input$var1), max(input$var1), length.out = 10),
    seq(min(input$var2), max(input$var2), length.out = 10)), 
    ...
 } )
==========

Silly example, but imaging having something go awry with lapply() (common for me). Now I need to execute it manually and replace every instance of input$soemthing with a real value.

Is there a way to automate this, or perhaps I don't understand debugging shiny apps at all and am going about this all wrong. I read the run & debug bit on the tutorial, but I don't think that's what I want. I'm new enough to R that just seeing the error message isn't going to help me. I end up wanting to see the results of head() or str() on an object created in the app, but I can't get to it since it's only running in shiny, not the session. Thus, I have to manually recreate an analog to my shiny code in the session itself, and run into the issue of replacing all my references to input$.


Thanks,
John

messages.author: 2ed19a7addb843f5
messages.subject: Re: Making input object accessible to R session for debugging help?
parts:
A way to do this is to create an input data.frame in your R session.

input = data.frame(var1 = testvalue1,var2 = testvalue2)

Then you can run the code from your server as is. Changing inputs is also easy.

messages.subject: Re: Making input object accessible to R session for debugging help?
